title: Informal Conjecture (error term in Proposition 1.4)
statement_text: Let $m<k$ and $t$ be integers with $t=1$ or $k=m+1$, let $H$ be a graph with $\chi(H)=k$, and let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices with minimum degree $\delta(G)>(1-\epsilon)n$ for a suitable $\epsilon=\epsilon(m,t,k)>0$ and $n$ large. The authors prove that every $H$-free subgraph of $G$ with the maximum possible number of copies of $K_m(t)$ can be made $(k-1)$-colorable by deleting $o(n^2)$ edges, and believe that the error term $o(n^2)$ can be improved to $O(n^{2-\delta})$ for some $\delta := \delta(H)>0$.
context_text: $K_m(t)$ is the $t$-blow-up of $K_m$, obtained by replacing each vertex of $K_m$ by an independent set of size $t$ and each edge by a complete bipartite graph ($K_m(1)=K_m$). For a host graph $G$, $\mathcal{G}_{ex}(T,H)$ is the family of $H$-free subgraphs of $G$ with the maximum possible number of copies of $T$. A graph $H$ is edge critical if deleting some edge reduces its chromatic number. Generalizing results on Turán's theorem in host graphs of high minimum degree (Bondy–Shen–Thomassé–Thomassen, Balogh–Keevash–Sudakov, Alon–Shapira–Sudakov), the authors prove that if $H$ is edge critical with $\chi(H)=k>m$ and $\delta(G)\ge(1-\epsilon)n$, then every member of $\mathcal{G}_{ex}(K_m,H)$ is $(k-1)$-colorable, and similarly every member of $\mathcal{G}_{ex}(K_m(t),H)$ is $m$-colorable when $\chi(H)=m+1$. These cannot be directly generalized to non-edge-critical $H$, since one can add an edge to any $(k-1)$-partite graph without creating such an $H$, which is why only an approximate statement (deleting few edges) holds in general. The belief is supported by a theorem of Alon and Sudakov: if $\chi(H)=k\ge3$, $|V(H)|=h$, and $G$ is an $H$-free graph with $\delta(G)\ge(1-\frac{3}{3k-4}+o(1))n$, then deleting $O(n^{2-1/(4(k-1)^{2/3}h)})$ edges makes $G$ $(k-1)$-colorable.
notes: Stated in the introduction as 'we believe'; Section 6 (concluding remarks and open problems) is not present in the extracted text and may contain additional items.
paper_title: $H$-free subgraphs of dense graphs maximizing the number of cliques and their blow-ups
